newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Five Jamaicans nabbed in Caymans cocaine busts.
newsitem.headline: Five Jamaicans nabbed in Caymans cocaine busts.

text.p: A Jamaican man nearly died when a packet of cocaine he had ingested for a drug-smuggling run burst inside his stomach, Cayman Islands drugs officials said on Tuesday.

He was one of five Jamaicans arrested on Monday as they attempted to enter the Caymans on a flight from Jamaica. A total of 6.6 pounds (three kilos) of cocaine with a street value of about $1 million in the United States was seized.
"He is lucky to be alive because a package broke inside him," Drugs Task Force superintendant Derek Haines said.

The alleged smuggler and another Jamaican passed more than 90 packets of cocaine from their digestive systems at the hospital, Haines said. Two others allegedly had cocaine stuffed in their shoes while a fifth man ejected 30 plastic-wrapped packets of the drug from his stomach.
In the past three years two Jamaicans have died when cocaine burst in their stomachs, Haines said. The drugs were destined for the United States, he added.
Drug traffickers believe passengers on flights from the Cayman Islands are less likely to be searched at U.S. airports than those arriving from Jamaica.
